content: An asphalt or concrete roadway is classified as impassable and hazardous if standing or flowing floodwater exceeds 6 inches (15 cm) in depth, or if structural pavement washout has occurred. Emergency response vehicles cannot safely navigate roads with contiguous water covering lane markings. High-water marks and submerged curbs indicate immediate hazard status.

Level 1 (Affected) indicates minor, non-structural damage. Buildings show cosmetic surface staining, superficial siding displacement, or minor roof shingle loss covering less than 5% of the total surface. Structural frame, exterior load-bearing walls, and foundation remain completely intact and secure.

Level 2 (Minor Damage) encompasses buildings with water lines below 18 inches in living areas, damage to non-structural elements (soffits, fascia, window glazing), or partial roof covering loss between 5% and 25%. The primary structure remains habitable and can be repaired rapidly without complete rebuild.

Level 3 (Major Damage) indicates substantial structural failure where the property is uninhabitable. Evidenced by water lines exceeding 18 inches above the first floor, major roof collapse or puncture exceeding 25% of surface area, wall displacement, or compromised load-bearing partitions. Extensive professional rehabilitation is required before re-occupancy.

Level 4 (Destroyed) indicates total structural collapse or damage so severe that repair is economically and structurally unfeasible. Characterized by complete roof framing detachment, collapse of foundation walls, washed-out structural piers, or only the slab remaining visible in aerial and UAV imagery.

topic: Inland Water Bodies and Flooded Vegetation
content: Artificial and natural water surfaces exhibit low reflectance in the near-infrared and shortwave-infrared spectra. In high-resolution RGB aerial orthophotos, floodwater appears dark blue, brown, or green depending on sediment load and suspended particulate concentration. Flooded vegetation occurs where tree canopies or reed beds emerge from contiguous standing water.

topic: Urban Built-up Infrastructure and Residential Zones
content: Built-up areas comprise residential structures, paved transportation networks, and commercial complexes. In high-resolution UAV orthomosaics (GSD < 5 cm), residential roof structures typically show rectangular or pitched geometries with asphalt shingle, tile, or metal cladding, bounded by parcel fences, driveways, and street curbs.

topic: Aerial Perspective, Sun Glint, and Shadow Occlusion
content: High-resolution nadir and oblique aerial imagery are prone to specular reflection (sun glint) across water surfaces and deep shadow occlusion cast by tall structures or mature tree canopies. When sub-surface building features or submerged roadway substrates are obscured by dark shadow cast or turbid sediment, visual confirmation cannot be validated with certainty, mandating epistemic abstention.

Drainage ditches, culverts, and retention basins are designated as critical hydrological mitigation features. In aerial surveys, failure or overtopping of retention embankments results in radial debris deposition and contiguous backwater pooling into adjacent residential and industrial rights-of-way.

A passenger vehicle or light truck is considered stranded and hazardous when floodwater reaches hubcap height or higher. Vehicles submerged to window level indicate severe local inundation exceeding 2.5 feet (75 cm), signifying that evacuation routes along that corridor are completely cut off.
